newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FRUSTRATED CZECH SENATOR SAYS PORN SMEAR COST HIM.
newsitem.headline: FRUSTRATED CZECH SENATOR SAYS PORN SMEAR COST HIM.

text.p: A southeast Prague candidate said on Monday he would have won a seat in the new Czech Senate outright instead of having to face a runoff next weekend if it was not for a pornographic smear campaign against him.

Zdenek Klausner, candidate for the ruling right-wing Civic Democratic Party (ODS), said a widely-circultated photograph showing a man with his face involved in a group sex act cost him at least the 1.4 percent of the vote he needed to win.
He said he went to the police to prove that the man in the picture -- which was anonymously mailed in plain envelopes to between 5,000 to 10,000 local homes, businesses, and the media -- was not him.
"Right after citizens began telephoning that they received (the picture) I went with the police for various comparative measurements," Klausner was quoted as saying by the CTK agency.
"That night I received the statement of the criminal department that (the picture) was a forgery."
Klausner, aged 49, received 48.63 percent of the vote, just short of the 50 percent needed to win the seat in the first round.
He now must face former Czech parliament chairwoman Dagmar Buresova, a candidate from the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL) who won 21.44 percent of the vote last weekend.
"I would speculate that the same campaign against me will continue in the next week," Klausner said.
Police are looking into claims that the picutre was part of an organised smear campaign against Klausner, but it is not yet clear who was responsible for the mailings.
ODS, led by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, topped the first round of the elections winning three seats outright, with 76 candidates in the runoff elections out of 81 total constituencies.
